title: Epstein circle's gravity interest as an electrogravitics/UFO quest

tellings.quote: Therefore, I suspect that the interest in gravity is an interest in electrogravitics and you know the Townson Brown effect and basically it's all part of the UFO phenomenon that they're trying to crack.

tellings.page: section "“I wish I never met him.”", paragraph 10
tellings.quote: Jeffrey Epstein was also obsessed with physics research and technological developments directed toward defying gravity. In other words, he was interested in electrogravitics or what is believed to be the power and propulsion system of UFOs.

plain: The financier Jeffrey Epstein was fixated on physics research into defying gravity, and the researcher and philosopher Jason Jorjani suspects this was really a hunt for electrogravitics, the idea of controlling gravity with electricity, which he describes as what is believed to be the power and propulsion system of UFOs. On the show Jorjani tells Michels he "suspects" it, links it to an effect named after the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown, and says it is "all part of the UFO phenomenon that they're trying to crack." In his own essay Ocean Outlaw: A Portrait of Ghislaine Maxwell, about Epstein's associate Ghislaine Maxwell and published on 29 July 2025, he states it plainly as fact ("In other words, he was interested in electrogravitics") and does not mention Brown at all.

discussion.by: Ocean Outlaw: A Portrait of Ghislaine Maxwell
discussion.text: In the piece Jorjani states Epstein's interest in electrogravitics as a fact ("In other words, he was interested in electrogravitics"), not as the suspicion he voices on the podcast, and he does not name Thomas Townsend Brown or the Biefeld-Brown effect.
